newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 10.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- TAXMAN WILL IGNORE FREE SHARES

The Inland Revenue confirmed that members of the Halifax and other converting building societies will not be required to pay tax on their share bonuses. The gains can be shifted into personal equity plans, which allow all gains to be made free from tax.
-- HANSEN AIMS TO SCORE 200 MILLION STG INVESTMENT GOAL

Match of the Day commentator Alan Hansen has launched Britain's first football fund. The fund will be run by merchant bank Singer & Freidlander, who expects it to attract 30 million stg next month and 200 million stg by the end of the year.
-- WEINSTOCK AIDE QUITS IN NEW GEC SHAKE-UP

Top management changes continued at GEC yesterday with the announcement of the departure of key Lord Weinstock aide Malcom Bates, deputy managing director. Insiders denied any differences between Bates and managing director George Simpson.
THE TIMES
-- MERRETT NOT TO WORK AT LLOYD'S AGAIN AFTER 1.0 MLN STG DEAL

Former deputy chairman of Lloyd's of London, Stephen Merrett is to pay one million stg in damages and will never work at Lloyd's again, following accusations of negligence, incompetence and dereliction of duty made in a High Court two years ago.
-- SEARS WARNING PUTS STRONG'S JOB AT RISK
Chief executive of Sears Liam Strong is under growing pressure from institutional shareholders to resign following a profit warning issued by the retail group yesterday.
-- M&S SHOPPING FOR PROPERTY

Marks & Spencer is poised to buy one of Edinburgh's biggest shopping centres. The 300,000 sq ft Gyle Shopping centre will cost Marks & Spencer 122 million stg from the city council and will be the groups first venture into becoming a landlord.
THE GUARDIAN
-- KOHL DEFIES EURO GLOOM

The German government reported slower growth, a worse than expected budget deficit and the worst unemployment levels since the 1930s. Chancellor Helmut Kohl tried to put a brave face on, claiming that the economy was set for recovery, but indications from within German and from Britain were that Europe's biggest economy was now unlikely to fulfil the Maastricht conversion criteria for a single currency.
-- PROSPEROUS YEAR IN STORE FOR RETAILERS

According to the Confederation of British Industry, December's sales figures were the best for three years, although the pace of expansion slowed compared to the previous month. The continuing consumer boom and the strength of the pound, which broke through the nine French franc-barrier for the first time in three years yesterday, look set to dominate Wednesday's meeting between Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George when they will discuss interest rates.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- INSURERS FAIL TO CUT CHARGES AFTER DISCLOSURE

The Personal Investment Authority said insurance companies are still refusing to cut charges on their policies, two years after rules forcing disclosure of costs were passed. A survey by the authority shows most companies still charge the same as last year.
-- MORTGAGE LENDING HIGHEST IN YEARS

A Barclays Bank survey released showed that mortgage lending last year reached a six-year record of 71 billion stg. The survey showed there were more than twice as many home buyers as sellers on the market. The survey coincided with an increase in housing starts of 15 percent in the three months to November.
-- KLEINWORT FINED 30,000 STG POUNDS BY SFA

Kleinwort Benson Securities has been fined 30,000 stg, plus 7,900 stg in costs, by the Securities and Futures Authority after admitting failures in its internal controls. Two former registered representatives of the firm mismarked positions which led to Kleinwort showing a paper loss of approximately 50,000 stg.
